extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner/practitioner guidance on reissue applications, certificates of correction (Office and applicant mistakes), public access, and correction of assignees' and inventors' names under relevant statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to Utility Patent via Reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent cannot be converted to a utility patent via reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 251 requires that the 'patent is, through error without any deceptive intention, deemed wholly or partly inoperative or invalid, by reason of a defective specification or drawing, or by reason of the patentee claiming more or less than he had a right to claim in the patent'; however, the design patent (for which the reissue application would be filed) is not wholly or partly inoperative or invalid. There is no error in the design patent. Also, converting a design patent to a utility patent will, in most instances, involve the introduction of new matter into the patent. The disclosure of a design patent is not directed to how the invention is made and used, and the introduction of new matter is required to bridge this gap and provide support for the utility patent. Accordingly, the examiner should consider rejections based on the introduction of new matter under 35 U.S.C. 251 and lack of enablement and/or description under 35 U.S.C. 112, when a reissue application is filed to convert a design patent to a utility patent. Further, the term of a design patent may not be extended by reissue; a reissue that would extend the term should be rejected as failing to comply with 35 U.S.C. 251.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to Design Patent via Reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility patent cannot be converted to a design patent via reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 251 requires an error rendering the patent wholly or partly inoperative or invalid; a utility patent is not inoperative or invalid simply for being utility. Conversion to a design patent would exempt the existing utility patent from maintenance fees and there is no statutory basis for such exemption. See also the prohibition on extending patent term discussed under conversion to utility patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Reissue (35 U.S.C. 252)
rubrics_metrics.description: The surrender of the original patent shall take effect upon the issue of the reissued patent, and every reissued patent shall have the same effect and operation in law as if originally granted in the amended form; where claims are substantially identical the reissue constitutes a continuation with effect from the original date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 252 also provides for intervening rights: 'Absolute' intervening rights are available for parties who, prior to the grant of a reissue, made, purchased, offered to sell, used, or imported anything patented by the reissued patent; 'equitable' intervening rights may be provided where substantial preparation was made before grant. Multiple reissue application situations can affect when surrender of the original patent takes effect (e.g., surrender occurs when at least one reissued patent is granted and there are no pending reissue applications). See cited cases (BIC Leisure Prods.; McCormick; Pfizer v. Apotex; Peck v. Collins) and MPEP § 1450 for divisional reissue details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access to Reissue Applications (37 CFR 1.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue applications are open to inspection by the general public and filings of reissue applications are announced in the Official Gazette, providing the public an opportunity to submit information pertinent to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing of a continued prosecution application (CPA) of a design reissue will not be announced in the Official Gazette. Reissue application files are accessible via Patent Center on the USPTO website; members of the public can view entire reissue application file history. Announcement in the Official Gazette gives interested members of the public an opportunity to submit information to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Correction for Office Mistake (35 U.S.C. 254; 37 CFR 1.322)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may issue a certificate of correction for a mistake in a patent incurred through the fault of the Office, where the mistake is clearly disclosed by the records of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may act at the request of the patentee/assignee, sua sponte for Office-discovered mistakes, or on information supplied by a third party. The Office is not obligated to act on third-party submissions and will not make such papers of record nor retain them. The Office may decline to issue a certificate where the meaning is obvious from context and instead place correspondence in the patent file. Certificates should be requested only for errors of consequence; minor typographical errors that are readily apparent to one skilled in the art can be made of record by letter instead (no fee). It is strongly advised to submit the text of the correction on form PTO/SB/44 (PTO-1050) and to identify the location of the error by column and line number or claim and line number. Use the specified document description when filing electronically and address submissions to the Certificates of Correction Branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-Party Information on Patent Mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties may submit information about mistakes in patents, but they do not have standing to demand issuance or refusal of a certificate of correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.322(a)(2) clarifies third parties do not have standing to demand Office action; the Office may accept information from third parties and may issue a certificate on its own initiative based on such information, but has no obligation to respond or act. Papers submitted by third parties under this section will not be made of record or retained. If the Office chooses to act sua sponte, it will notify the patentee and afford opportunity to be heard. Third-party requests should be clearly labeled 'Third-Party Request for Certificate of Correction' and should not be filed via the USPTO patent electronic filing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited Issuance of Certificates of Correction (Office Error)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will expedite processing and granting of patentee requests for certificates of correction where the request is accompanied by evidence showing the error is attributable solely to the Office and the matter is clearly disclosed in Office records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for expedited consideration: submit text on PTO/SB/44 (not necessary in duplicate); identify location by column/line or claim/line; provide documentation unequivocally supporting patentee's assertion (e.g., relevant pages, photocopied correspondence dated and received by the Office, Examiners' responses regarding entry of amendments, receipts, manuscript pages) so the request can be processed without the patent file. Where only part of a request can be approved, patentee will receive a Notification of Approval-in-part and may request reconsideration. If determined the Office was not responsible, accelerated issuance cannot be anticipated. Use the prescribed document description when filing electronically and address submissions to the Certificates of Correction Branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Correction for Applicant's Mistake (35 U.S.C. 255; 37 CFR 1.323)
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate of correction for an applicant's mistake may be issued where the mistake is clerical, typographical, or of minor character, was not the fault of the Office, was made in good faith, and the correction would not constitute new matter or require reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two statutory requirements per In re Arnott: (1) the mistake must be clerical, typographical, or of minor character; (2) the proposed correction must not involve changes that would constitute new matter or require reexamination. Mistakes affecting claim scope (e.g., broadening a claim) generally are not 'minor' and should be corrected by reissue rather than certificate of correction. Clerical mistakes that are manifest from the patent file are typically correctable; errors requiring evidence outside the file are likely not manifest and not correctable. Benefit or foreign priority claim errors typically require petitions (37 CFR 1.78(e), 1.55(e)), not certificates. Fees for applicant mistake corrections are set in 37 CFR 1.20(a) (and for inventorship corrections 1.20(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Assignees' Names and Assignment Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignee information should be provided on the Fee(s) Transmittal Form (PTOL-85B) item 3 to be printed on the issued patent; providing assignee data on PTOL-85B does not change applicant of record unless appropriate request under 37 CFR 1.46(c) is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment data printed on the patent is based solely on information supplied with PTOL-85B (or equivalent) on the date the issue fee is paid; assignment information submitted after issue fee payment will not be printed. Requests submitted after payment of the issue fee or after issuance to issue the patent in the name of the assignee must: (A) state that the assignment was submitted for recordation under 37 CFR 3.11 before issuance; (B) include a request for a certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.323 with the fee in 37 CFR 1.20(a); and (C) include the processing fee in 37 CFR 1.17(i). Requests not complying with 37 CFR 3.81(b) will not be granted. Mistakenly adding assignee information on PTOL-85B is not correctable via certificate of correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Named Inventor (35 U.S.C. 256; 37 CFR 1.324)
rubrics_metrics.description: When through error an inventor is named or omitted in an issued patent, the Director may, on application of all the parties and assignees (or on court order), issue a certificate correcting inventorship, subject to statutory and regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For requests filed on or after September 16, 2012, a petition must be accompanied by: (1) a statement from each person being added and each person currently named either agreeing to the change or stating no disagreement (37 CFR 1.324(b)(1)); (2) a statement from all assignees agreeing to the change, complying with 37 CFR 3.73(c) (37 CFR 1.324(b)(2)); and (3) the fee in 37 CFR 1.20(b). Correction under 35 U.S.C. 256 requires application of all parties and assignees and thus cannot be waived. If an inventor is unavailable or refuses, consider filing a reissue (inventor's statement not required for a non-broadening reissue to correct inventorship). Requests to correct inventorship in interferences or contested PTAB cases must be made by motion under relevant rules (37 CFR 41.121(a)(2) or 42.22) and comply with 1.324. Use form PTO/SB/44 when submitting requests to correct inventorship in a patent; if the completed form is not provided, provide names and residence information for Office printing. Name changes (e.g., legal name change) after issuance are not correctable by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 254/255 nor by 35 U.S.C. 256, and are inappropriate grounds for an inventorship correction.
